topology_reasoning.device: Symmetric compact interferometric/coupled structure drawn as one material layer: an outer closed racetrack/oval guide surrounds two mirrored inner rails. The inner rails have widened slotted interaction blocks with two rectangular windows per rail and angled access tapers from the outer side regions.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: The outer loop and mirrored upper/lower rails define a compact two-arm path/coupler-like topology. Optical behavior is controlled by the guide width, the rail separation, the central slotted interaction length, the slot dimensions, the taper/access length, and any differential arm length. The baseline image is symmetric, so the differential length knob starts at zero.
topology_reasoning.primitive_plan: Use gf.Path + extrude for the outer oval loop and access guides, rectangles for the widened slotted interaction bodies and rectangular windows, and boolean union/subtraction to create the final layer-(1,0) material. No raw polygons or device stencil components.

iterations.change_made: Initial primitive model: constant-width gf.Path ellipse for outer loop, path access guides, rectangular slotted interaction bodies.
Replaced constant-width ellipse with a rectangle-primitive superellipse annulus so outer and inner loop boundaries can be tuned independently.
Flattened the annulus exterior, enlarged the inner annulus cutout, and slightly enlarged the rectangular slots.
Reduced the annulus side overshoot and raised the access guide entry points to restore the central gap.
Lifted access guides further, shrank the annulus side profile, and enlarged the slots; this improved precision but lost too much connector recall.
Tried midpoint access-guide placement with restored annulus strength and enlarged windows; did not beat iteration 4.
